title: FX option expiries for 11 September 10am New York cut
body: USD/JPY: 154.00 US$2.86bn 153.00 US$2.74bn 152.00 US$1.66bn EUR/USD: 1.1575 EUR1.44bn 1.1600 EUR996.2mn 1.1500 EUR947mn AUD/USD: 0.7150 AUD657.4mn 0.7250 AUD622.1mn 0.7110 AUD543.5mn USD/CAD: 1.3900 US$693.8mn 1.3800 US$535mn 1.3950 US$319.7mn GBP/USD: 1.3630 GBP565.4mn 1.3500 GBP540mn Q&A: FX option expiries What exactly is an FX option expiry? An FX option gives its holder the right, though not the requirement, to buy or sell one currency for another at an agreed rate, called the strike, on or before a set date. That date is the expiry. Why can a large expiry influence the spot market? It largely comes down to hedging. Banks and dealers who have written these options typically hedge their exposure by trading the underlying currency pair. As spot price approaches the strike, those hedges often need adjusting, which can generate extra buying or selling in the spot market. Does a large expiry automatically mean price will move towards the strike? Not necessarily, and this is worth remembering. An expiry is context, not a signal. Say EUR/USD sits at 1.1600 with a large expiry at 1.1800: that expiry likely won't have much sway on its own. But if EUR/USD is trading at 1.1790 with only a few hours left before the option lapses, the strike becomes far more relevant to price action. title: New Zealand Manufacturing Momentum Eases as Business NZ PMI Slips in August
body: New Zealand's manufacturing sector showed a modest loss of momentum in August, with the Business NZ Performance of Manufacturing Index (PMI) easing to 53.1, down from 54.3 in July 2026. The latest reading, updated on 10 September 2026, indicates that while the sector remains in expansionary territory, growth has moderated. The August 2026 figure suggests that activity is still improving overall, as PMI readings above 50 signal expansion. However, the decline from July's level points to a softer pace of growth heading into the latter part of the year, potentially reflecting more cautious business conditions or emerging demand headwinds. Investors and policymakers will be watching subsequent releases closely to assess whether this slowdown is temporary or the beginning of a more sustained cooling in New Zealand's manufacturing outlook. title: Oil Tops $103 as Middle East Risks Mount
body: Crude oil prices climbed above $103 a barrel on Thursday, the highest level since May 19, as escalating tensions in the Middle East stoked fears of prolonged disruptions to global energy supplies. Top White House advisers reportedly discussed with President Donald Trump the possibility that the war with Iran could continue beyond Inauguration Day in January 2029. The conflict widened this week as Iran's Houthi allies in Yemen struck several energy facilities in Saudi Arabia, intensifying concerns over regional stability. Saudi Arabia's crude oil output fell sharply in August 2026, down by roughly 1.9 million barrels per day. Iran reported attacks on US warships and tankers in the Persian Gulf, while Washington said it had targeted 10 Iranian tankers. Adding to the upward pressure on prices, oil tanker freight rates surged to record highs, and US crude inventories declined by 300,000 barrels in the week ended September 4. In contrast, the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) raised its forecast for US crude oil production in 2027 to 14.3 million barrels per day, signaling expectations of robust output despite geopolitical uncertainties. title: Brazilian Stocks Rise on Election Outlook
body: The Ibovespa climbed 1.4% to close at 188,269 on Thursday, reversing earlier losses as investors priced in a higher likelihood of a change in power in October's presidential election. Recent polls have shown Flávio Bolsonaro gaining ground in the race, and shifting odds on Polymarket added further momentum to Thursday's move. Markets tend to associate a potential Flávio Bolsonaro victory with tighter fiscal policy, even as high domestic interest rates and subdued business activity continue to cloud the economic outlook. Gains were broad-based, with major banks leading the advance: Itaú rose 1.8%, Bradesco jumped 3.9%, and Banco do Brasil gained 2.8%. Utilities also finished higher, with Sabesp up 2.2%. Rede D'Or outperformed, rising 3.1%. In commodities, Petrobras advanced 1.4% on the back of higher oil prices, while Vale fell 1.1% amid a decline in iron ore prices. title: Fed Balance Sheet Edges Higher to $6.741 Trillion, Signaling Ongoing Tight but Stable Policy Stance
body: The U.S. Federal Reserve's balance sheet inched up to $6.741 trillion, according to data updated on 10 September 2026, marking a modest increase from the previous level of $6.737 trillion. The change underscores that while the Fed is no longer expanding its asset holdings at the pace seen during earlier crisis responses, its balance sheet remains elevated by historical standards. For markets, the slight uptick suggests the central bank continues to manage liquidity and maturing securities in a way that keeps financial conditions stable rather than aggressively tightening further through balance sheet reduction alone. Investors watching the trajectory of the Fed's assets may interpret the latest data as a sign that, for now, the central bank is favoring a steady, incremental approach over abrupt shifts in its quantitative stance. title: Canadian Stocks Slide on Inflation Fears
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index declined 1.1% to close at 35,506 on Thursday, as rising oil prices and higher bond yields intensified inflation concerns. Crude prices surged amid heightened fears of prolonged energy supply disruptions, following the largest wave of attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz by Washington and Tehran on Wednesday. Global bond yields climbed on worries that inflation will remain elevated, adding further pressure on equity markets. Weakness in precious and base metals also weighed on the index. Gold's pullback hit miners, with Agnico Eagle down 2.8%, Barrick off 2.3%, and WPM sliding 3.7%. Copper prices retreated as well, pushing Hudbay down 7.3% and Capstone 9.3%. Enbridge fell 3.7% after announcing the acquisition of Tallgrass Energy's crude oil business, including a majority stake in the Pony Express Pipeline and related assets. title: Argentina Monthly Inflation Eases in August
body: Argentina's consumer price index rose 1.7% month-on-month in August 2026, down from 2.1% in July and in line with market expectations. The largest monthly increase was recorded in housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels (2.8%), followed by education (2.5%). Prices in recreation and culture were unchanged, while clothing and footwear declined by 0.6%. Food and non-alcoholic beverages made the biggest contribution to monthly inflation across all regions, driven by higher prices for vegetables, tubers, legumes, fruit, bread and cereals. Regulated prices increased 2.2%, mainly reflecting higher costs for electricity, gas, public transportation and private healthcare. Seasonal prices fell 0.9%, as lower prices for tour packages and clothing were partly offset by increases in vegetables, tubers, legumes and fruit. Year-to-date inflation reached 21.3%, while core CPI rose 1.8% in the month. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: US Stocks Pressured by Higher Yields
body: US stock indices closed lower on Thursday as a jump in oil and fuel prices pushed Treasury yields higher and raised concerns about corporate profit margins. The S&P 500 fell 0.6%, the Nasdaq lost 1.1%, and the Dow declined by 316 points. Producer prices rose 0.4% month-over-month in August, as the war in Iran drove wholesale energy costs higher. Oil and fuel benchmarks have climbed further since the start of September amid renewed escalation in the conflict and stronger demand from Asia, adding pressure on equities ahead of a potential Federal Reserve rate hike next week. Chipmakers retreated on worries about their sensitivity to rising long-term borrowing costs, with Nvidia down 2.3%, Micron off 4.9%, AMD lower by 3.4%, and Intel sliding 5.6%. Oracle fell 5.4% ahead of its earnings release after the close. Meta (-1.4%) and Palantir (-2.2%) also ended the session in negative territory. In contrast, Apple gained 3.6%, trimming Wednesday's losses after unveiling a slate of new products, including the foldable iPhone Duo.
